procedure.description: neuroplasty and/or transposition, median nerve at carpal tunnel

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Prairie Commons Medicaid Plan denied the claim for CPT 64721 (neuroplasty and/or transposition, median nerve at carpal tunnel) with date of service 2026-03-03. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish failure of conservative treatment or electrodiagnostic confirmation.

criteria.text: Symptoms consistent with carpal tunnel syndrome, such as nocturnal paresthesias in the median nerve distribution with a positive Tinel or Phalen sign, present for at least 6 weeks.
Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management including neutral wrist splinting, together with NSAIDs, activity modification, or a corticosteroid injection.
Electrodiagnostic testing (nerve conduction study or electromyography) confirming median neuropathy at the wrist, unless thenar atrophy or constant sensory loss is present.

chart.text: From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

63 year old woman here for the right hand, referred by the PCP. Works on a keyboard all day. Discussed carpal tunnel release, open versus endoscopic, recovery. Her history otherwise: mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year, seasonal allergies. Surgeries: a C-section. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works retail. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. 8 months of numbness and tingling in the thumb, index, and middle fingers on the right, wakes her at night, shakes it out. Positive Tinel at the right wrist, Phalen positive in about 20 seconds. Some early thenar weakness, no atrophy yet. Gave her a wrist splint to wear at night and told her to try ibuprofen, and we will see.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Vitamin D came back 23. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 4 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 2.6, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.

Nerve conduction study, right upper extremity. Median sensory peak latency 4.8 milliseconds across the wrist, prolonged. Median motor distal latency 6.4 milliseconds, prolonged. Ulnar normal. Consistent with moderate right median neuropathy at the wrist.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Blood pressure check. 125 over 84 today, 130 over 79 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 15 and 19. No ocular pathology noted.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Back to review the plan for the right hand. Still symptomatic. Wants to proceed. Vitals today 128 over 68, pulse 64. Says the splint is too hot and she has not been wearing it. Has not tried the ibuprofen regularly either.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Nurse call. Patient had questions about time off work after surgery and whether she needs someone at home the first night. Answered both, she will arrange it.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.

Here with a cough and congestion for 6 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Interval visit. Nothing new since last time, symptoms as described before, she is managing. Went over the plan again and answered questions from her spouse.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.
Pre-op. Consent signed for right open carpal tunnel release under local with sedation. Marked.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

expected.note: The chart raises crit-2 (conservative) but does not satisfy it; the mention is a plan or a shortfall, not completed treatment or a met threshold.
